item.title: The p word
item.author: rhlvenugopal@gmail.com (xxxx)
item.description: So, a group of 124 prominent researchers in the field of consciousness published a one-page preprint titled The Integrated Information Theory of Consciousness as Pseudoscience to express their concerns about the media hype of Integrated Information Theory (IIT), and a heated discussion ensued on Twitter. This is a collection of threads that would be valuable for anyone interested in gathering well-rounded opinions around this preprint. I’m hoping that the flame wars will encourage researchers to rethink their approaches

item.title: What is the procedure for getting a PhD in NIMHANS? Part 1
item.author: rhlvenugopal@gmail.com (xxxx)
item.description: There are three ways to gain PhD admission. Path 1 — Institutional Fellowship: The institute funds up to three fellowship seats per department (not all departments offer these). To get in, you must pass both an entrance exam and an interview. This is the most competitive route. Entrance exams typically consist of MCQs from the department’s field. Path 2 — External Fellowship: Secure your own external fellowship (UGC, CSIR, ICMR, etc.

item.title: What is the procedure for getting a PhD in NIMHANS? Part 2
item.author: rhlvenugopal@gmail.com (xxxx)
item.description: Download the latest entrance prospectus from the NIMHANS website. It covers eligibility requirements, course duration, fees, stipend, number of seats, and more. The typical timeline: the announcement goes out in the first week of January, followed by the entrance exam, interview, selection announcement, admission, and course commencement by the first week of July. Almost every faculty member has a government- or institution-funded project. These projects typically last three to five years and have openings for JRFs/SRFs or research associates.

item.title: What is the procedure for getting a PhD in NIMHANS? Part 3
item.author: rhlvenugopal@gmail.com (xxxx)
item.description: Starting the first week of January each year, watch the NIMHANS website closely. The notification and online application are released in the first week of January. There are limits on how many courses you can apply for. Review the prospectus for details on new courses, eligibility requirements, required documents, etc. Reach out to current students for insights on the course structure and exam format. Prepare for the exam, held in the last week of March.

item.title: How to prepare for a masters or PhD in Neuroscience
item.author: rhlvenugopal@gmail.com (xxxx)
item.description: The exam syllabus is manageable even for someone without a biology or medical background, provided you put in consistent reading and effort. Get Instant Notes in Neurosciences. Read it from the first page to the last. If you feel lost, don’t worry — that’s normal. Estimated completion time: 14 days. Reread the neuroscience/physiology sections of the CBSE biology textbook. Estimated completion time: 7 days. Dale Purves’ Neuroscience is an easy, quick read to build a high-level understanding of the subject.

item.title: How is the course? Part 1 | MPhil
item.author: rhlvenugopal@gmail.com (xxxx)
item.description: MPhil Neurophysiology and MPhil Neuroscience were distinct courses with different objectives. My MPhil was in Neurosciences, and I’m currently completing my PhD in Neurophysiology. Nearly every academic and scientific event on campus is open to students, yet many overlook these opportunities. Examples include morbidity & mortality conferences, brain-cutting sessions, workshops, colloquia, and journal/seminar clubs. Just make sure they don’t clash with your course schedule. Plan ahead. Neurosciences students are assigned monthly rotations across different departments (Genetics, Neurochemistry, Pathology, Virology, Biophysics, Biostatistics, Neurophysiology, Neuropathology, etc.

item.title: How is the course? Part 2 | PhD
item.author: rhlvenugopal@gmail.com (xxxx)
item.description: The first month is a habituation period — students settle in and get oriented. Coursework, animal handling training, and research begin in the second month and continue for about three months. During this time, doctoral students rotate through various labs. They attend one seminar and one journal club each week, and are welcome to join the additional teaching sessions held for MPhil students. Each professor typically teaches two or three sessions in their area of expertise.

item.title: What is a career option?
item.author: rhlvenugopal@gmail.com (xxxx)
item.description: The opinions of these so-called motivational gurus, passion seekers, and career counsellors on how to define one’s career are about as useful as conversations over what colour parachutes are worth. The modern job market is so vast that it would be impossible to locate an ideal career path in a single lifetime. In order to raise best sellers, creators fabricate the bogeyman of the “passion driven world.” Passion is not a long-lost artefact that can be revived with enough blood and sweat.

item.title: About me
item.author: rhlvenugopal@gmail.com (xxxx)
item.description: Who am I? Greetings from my little corner of the cosmos. I’m a 37-year-old human who now resides in Bengaluru, India. I completed a PhD in Cognitive Neurosciences from the Centre for Consciousness Studies, NIMHANS. My life has been quite exciting, and the path has been somewhat stormy, in my opinion (and I loved that). I transitioned from the engineering world to the study of the brain and the psyche. For fun, I engage in a variety of orthogonal activities.
